conviction_note: Near non-result: the one company-level tension (Street Q4 revenue of $331-342M needs +11-15% y/y against the CFO's August remark that growth will not be double-digit, after two straight revenue misses) leans negative, while peer and LNG-FID proxies, a likely backlog ramp and a stock already 52% off its high lean positive; p_up 47 on an abs move of 12 (implied 14.5%, own median 8.0%) gives -0.72, close to the findings' sum of -0.6, and the direction will be set by Q4 orders and the FY27/data-center commentary, neither of which is visible before the print.
bar: Q4 FY26 (quarter to 2026-09-30) consensus: revenue $341.8M and EPS $1.58 from 5 analysts per FXEmpire (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/powl/earnings, read 2026-11-16); Benzinga shows $330.8M and $1.54-1.55; Earnings Whispers $1.52; Sidoti $1.59, cut from $1.78. Prior-year Q4 FY25 was revenue $298M and EPS $4.22 pre-split = $1.41 post-split (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80420/000008042025000145/ex991-powlq4xfy2025earning.htm). The two revenue sources disagree by about $11M but both imply double-digit y/y growth (+11% to +15%). The company gives no formal guidance. The only company framing is the CFO's August remark that revenue growth will not be double-digit. Because the bar spans two sources that disagree, the revenue finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 2.91M shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, about 4.0 days to cover on 729K average volume, about 8% of the 36.4M shares outstanding (https://massive.com/quote/powl, read 2026-11-16). It is rising: 2.4M on 9/15 and 2.72M on 9/30 at 5.5 DTC (via search snippet of curvedtrading/massive). Elevated but not crowded. The tape shows a 5-day run-up of +8.0%, a 20-day move of -7.7%, the price 52.5% below the 52-week high, and +6.5% intraday today ($142.72 to about $152; massive.com 11:41 ET). Insiders made about $69.5M of open-market sales over 12 months and no buys.

findings.finding: The Street's Q4 FY26 revenue bar is $331-342M, which is +11% to +15% y/y against $298M in Q4 FY25, and EPS of $1.52-1.59 is +8% to +13% against $1.41. In the 2026-08 Q3 call, answering a question about the Q3 revenue shortfall, CFO Metcalf said 'we're not going to see double-digit Vs probably given the backlog conversion rate' and also flagged 'some pressure on SG&A as we stand up these new facilities'. Revenue missed consensus in both Q2 ($296.6M, +6%) and Q3 ($311.7M against $321.5M expected, +9%), so a third single-digit quarter (at most about $327M) would miss the bar again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-08-03): revenue missed by 3% and EPS by 5% despite record orders. The stock fell 13.9% after hours and closed the window -3.8%. Q2 FY26 (2026-05-04): EPS missed ($1.25 against $1.35) and the stock still rose +9.2% on a $400M+ order. Q4 FY25: revenue and EPS beat, orders were flat, and the stock fell -11.3%. On this name the revenue line moves the stock less than orders do.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still models double-digit growth ($331-342M) after the CFO said it would not come. If the market had taken the remark at face value, the estimates would sit near $320-327M. Sidoti cut to $1.59 from $1.78, but the aggregators show no revenue cut to single-digit growth.
findings.independence: Consensus from https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/powl/earnings ($341.8M, Q3 miss of $311.7M against $321.5M). Q2 revenue from the Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080420/000008042026000063/ex991-powlq2xfy2026earning.htm. The counterweight is the backlog-conversion finding below, which points to a ramp, though mostly in FY27 rather than in this quarter.

findings.finding: The backlog conversion arithmetic implies a revenue ramp starting about now. At 2026-06-30 backlog was $2.4B, with 'just under $1.3B' (54%) convertible within 12 months, plus about $75M a quarter of book-and-burn. Applied a year ago, the same method gave about $0.87B (low-60s% of $1.4B) plus about $0.3B, which matched the roughly $1.16B actually recorded over Q4 FY25 to Q3 FY26. It now implies about $1.6B over the next four quarters, against $1.16B trailing (+35-40%). The Jacintoport yard (335k sq ft, 'well in excess of $100M' annualised) was due to finish by FY26 year end, and the $400M+ data center order burns over 2-2.5 years.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Powell gives no numeric guide. Its FY outlook language moved the stock in Q1 FY26 (+16.3%, record backlog, megaproject orders) and in Q2 FY26 (+9.2%). After the Q3 'not double-digit' remark the stock fell 3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades at about 27x trailing EPS after a 52% drawdown, and its price targets were cut (JPMorgan $300 to $250, Cantor $320 to $235). That is not the multiple of a name expected to grow revenue 35%+. If the market believed the arithmetic, the shares would not sit near a 52-week-low-relative level. This is my own inference from public numbers, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the finding above, but a different number (backlog convertibility rather than the CFO's growth remark). The Q3 8-K gives $2.4B backlog and the Jacintoport timing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080420/000008042026000103/ex991-powlq3xfy2026earning.htm. The two findings can both hold: a soft Q4 and a strong FY27.

findings.finding: Q4 orders will most likely lack a mega order of Q3's size. Q3 orders were $934M including a $400M+ data center order, and CEO Cope said 'Upwards of $400 million, there's not a lot in the pipeline that's that large... nothing in the near term', though he added that $100M+ commercial mega jobs are coming 'a little bit more frequent'. In Q4 FY25, the last quarter with no mega order, orders were $271M (+1%), backlog fell 2% q/q, and the stock fell 11.3% despite beating on revenue and EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders drive this stock: Q4 FY25 orders flat gave -11.3%; Q1 FY26 orders $439M (+63%) gave +16.3%; Q2 FY26 orders $490M plus the $400M post-quarter order gave +9.2%; Q3 FY26 record orders with a revenue miss gave -3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell side knows Q3 was inflated by one order, so a sequential drop is partly expected. What is not visible is where Q4 orders land against roughly $300M of book-and-burn plus normal flow. If the market were already positioned for a sub-1x book-to-bill, the stock would not have run +8% into the print.
findings.independence: The prior-year Q4 orders and backlog come from the Q4 FY25 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80420/000008042025000145/ex991-powlq4xfy2025earning.htm. The LNG FID finding below cuts the other way.

findings.finding: Three large US Gulf Coast LNG projects reached FID between March and June 2026: Venture Global CP2 Phase 2 (March 2026, $8.6B), Caturus Commonwealth LNG (May/June 2026) and Delfin FLNG phase one (June 3, 2026, $5B). Electrical-package orders usually follow FID by a few months, which falls in Powell's Jul-Sep Q4. Management called LNG 'very robust', and its Jacintoport expansion is aimed first at LNG power control rooms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LNG mega orders were part of the Q1 FY26 (+16.3%) and Q3 FY26 order announcements; there is no separate LNG-only reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy. No customer or Powell disclosure ties an award from these FIDs to Powell's Q4, and the EPC award flow is not aggregated. If the market had priced LNG order flow into Q4, Q4 order estimates would be visible in previews; I found none.
findings.independence: Commonwealth FID: https://gcaptain.com/13-billion-commonwealth-lng-project-gets-green-light-in-louisiana/ ; CP2 Phase 2: https://rbnenergy.com/daily-posts/analyst-insight/cp2-phase-2-reached-fid-last-week-poised-boost-lng-feedgas . This is a proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: Peer Eaton reported on 2026-11-03, after Powell last spoke. Electrical Americas sales were a record $4.2B (+22% organic), data center sales +54%, rolling-12-month orders +39%, segment backlog +33%, total electrical backlog over $20B (+46%), and 2026 organic growth guidance was raised to 13-15%. This read-through says North American electrical and data center demand held through Powell's Q4 and into October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Powell has traded with the AI-power basket: Vertiv, GE Vernova and Eaton fell 9-13% on 2026-11-04 and rose 5-10% on 2026-11-09, and POWL is +8% over 5 days.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer print was overwhelmed the next day by the post-midterm selloff, so its demand signal went largely unreflected in the basket. POWL is still about 52% below its high while Eaton's demand data is at records. A peer is still a proxy for Powell's engineered-to-order mix, though.
findings.independence: Electrical backlog detail from a 10-Q read: https://fourweekmba.com/ai-eaton-filing-electrical-backlog-reaches-20-4b-up-46/ . Shares the Eaton source; a proxy.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-04 the AI-power equipment basket fell 7-14% (Vertiv -12.9%, Eaton -9.9%, Quanta -11.7%) after the Texas governor-elect, who campaigned on pausing new data centers, won. Texas holds about 27% of planned US data-center power. Powell is Houston-based, its $400M+ behind-the-meter order spans at least five North American sites, and this call (2026-11-17) is the first time management can address the policy risk to its data center pipeline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior policy-shock print. Peers fell on 11-04 and partly rebounded on 11-09 (Vertiv +9.6%, GE Vernova +7.1%, Eaton +5.1%).
findings.why_not_priced: The basket has already moved on the headline, so the macro read is priced. What is not priced is Powell's own exposure: the share of its data center backlog in Texas is not disclosed, and the trefis piece notes no company has reported losing an order. The sign depends on the call, so the size is small with a wide band.
findings.independence: The basket moves are also reported at https://www.tikr.com/blog/vertiv-sinks-9-ge-vernova-down-8-as-democrats-win-congress-reviving-data-center-fears ; the Nov 9 rebound at https://www.trefis.com/articles/623883/vertiv-stock-at-200-is-the-power-trade-back/2026-11-10 . Macro-to-company and unconfirmed by Powell.

outside_window.finding: A new leased facility of about 300,000 sq ft is planned to produce from late Q2 or early Q3 FY27, a $70-100M greenfield decision is pending, and craft-labour tightness is expected to bite in 2027-28. All of these are multi-quarter capacity items whose effect on revenue lands well after the exit window, though the call may update the decision.

lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): revenue consensus comes from two sources that disagree by about $11M ($330.8M against $341.8M), so the revenue-bar finding was capped from -2.0 to -1.5 and print_vs_bar moved from -3.5 to -3.0.
